report:
### Conclusion
The claim is **true**. Clinical trial evidence demonstrates that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix) significantly reduces the risk of shingles (herpes zoster) in adults aged 70 years or older.

### Evidence Summary
* **High Clinical Efficacy:** The pivotal ZOE-70 phase 3 randomized trial showed that the vaccine significantly reduces herpes zoster and postherpetic neuralgia among adults aged 70 years or older (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/). Specific trial results demonstrated an efficacy rate of approximately 89.8% in this age group (https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/4-things-pharmacists-should-know-about-the-shingrix-vaccine).
* **Durable Protection:** Follow-up clinical analyses show that protection remains strong over time, with efficacy against herpes zoster measured at approximately 85% in adults aged 70 and older during the fourth year post-vaccination (https://shingrixhcp.com/efficacy-safety/mechanism-of-action/).
* **Medical Guidelines:** Based on its proven effectiveness across older demographics, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends a two-dose series of Shingrix for immunocompetent adults aged 50 and older, with no upper age limit (https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html).

In summary, robust scientific data disproves the view that the claim is false; the vaccine provides high, durable protection against shingles in adults 70 and older.
